collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager leaving for five days gives a friend five shells to count the days: count them down faithfully, or lose count.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is going on a journey along the coast for five days. Before (subject.he/she) leaves, (subject.he/she) gives (friend) five shells in a little pile. "One a day," (subject.he/she) says. "When they're gone, I'm home." It's a sweet idea. On the first morning (friend) looks at the pile and moves one shell aside.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: On the third day (child), a child, borrows the shells for a game. When they come back, there are seven. Nobody knows where the extra two came from. (friend) gives up counting and simply watches the path in the evenings. (subject) comes home on the fifth day, exactly when (subject.he/she) said, and is confused by the seven shells for weeks.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: Every morning (friend) moves one shell. Four. Three. Two. One. On the morning of the last shell, (friend.he/she) waits on the path all day. (subject) arrives at sunset, dusty and tired. "Five days exactly," (subject.he/she) says proudly. (friend) holds up the last shell. "I was getting worried."
